html:
The Battle of Lechfeld was fought on 10 August 955 near Augsburg in Bavaria, southern Germany. The German king Otto I beat a large army of Magyar horsemen and ended their raids on western Europe.

For about sixty years the Magyars, who had settled in Hungary, had raided Germany, Italy and France almost every year. In 955 they came in great force and besieged Augsburg. Otto marched to its relief with about 8,000 heavy cavalry from the duchies of East Francia and from Bohemia. Part of the Magyar army rode around his column and fell on the baggage at the rear, but stopped to loot and was driven off. Otto then charged the main body. The Magyars could not stand against armoured horsemen at close range and fled. Many were killed in the following days, and their captured leaders were hanged.

The Magyars never raided the west again. Within two generations they had become a settled Christian kingdom, Hungary. The victory made Otto the strongest ruler in Europe, and in 962 the pope crowned him emperor, the start of the Holy Roman Empire. The exact site is still debated.
